rows.quote: For the purpose of this MR study, we used ancestry‐specific pQTL summary‐level data for South Asian populations obtained from the UKBPPP. 4 Genetic associations of 2922 circulating plasma proteins were obtained from the UKBPPP for individuals of Central/South Asian (CSA) ancestry (N=920) and European ancestry (N=34 557). 4 Summary statistics of GWAS, respectively, for individuals of CSA ancestry and European ancestry on stroke (NCSA=3640 cases and 7672 controls; NEURopean =73 652 cases and 1 234 808 controls) and 4 subtypes including ischemic stroke (NCSA=3462 cases and 7672 controls, NEUROPEAN=62 100 cases and 1 234 808 controls), cardioembolic stroke (NCSA=596 cases and 7672 controls, NEUROPEAN=10 804 cases and 1 234 808 controls), large artery stroke (NCSA=705 cases and 7672 controls, NEUROPEAN=6399 cases and 1 234 808 controls), and small vessel stroke (NCSA=647 cases and 7672 controls, NEUROPEAN=6811 cases and 1 234 808 controls) were obtained from the GIGASTROKE consortium. 9 The studies used in our analysis were approved by their respective institutional review boards, and informed consent was provided by all participants.
rows.coder_note: The sentence names the ancestry-specific (CSA and European) GIGASTROKE stroke GWAS; the Data Availability sentence (pqtl_1:p002) gives them as GWAS Catalog GCST90104559-GCST90104563 and GCST90104539-GCST90104543, accessions no dictionary row lists (rules B, G). That accession sentence occurs twice in the source: citations pin refused it as ambiguous and the occurrence helper raised, so this dataset-naming sentence is pinned instead.

Passage p004 attributes the pQTL data to UKBPPP (entry 4, Sun 2023, a source with several dictionary rows) for both CSA ancestry (N=920, the ancestry-specific non-European row) and European ancestry (N=34 557, the exact N of the discovery row); the attributes identify two different rows for the one name, so no single row is identified.
